title: Blest Hour, When Mortal Man Retires
description: Blest Hour, When Mortal Man Retires in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Raffles wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 44 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Hour of Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest hour, when mor-tal man re-tires To hold com-mu-nion with his God, To send to heaven his warm de-sires, And lis-ten to the sa-cred word.

lines: Blest hour, when mortal man retires
To hold communion with his God,
To send to heaven his warm desires,
And listen to the sacred word.
Blest hour, when earthly cares resign
Their empire o'er his anxious breast,
While, all around, the calm divine
Proclaims the holy day of rest.
Blest hour, when God himself draws nigh,
Well pleased his people's voice to hear,
And wipe away the mourner's tear.
Blest hour! for, where the Lord resorts,
Foretastes of future bliss are given,
And mortals find his earthly courts
The house of God, the gate of heaven.

licence: Public domain: Thomas Raffles died in 1863.
credits: Words by Thomas Raffles (1788–1863), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
